title: AlphaGenome Atlas maps predicted effects for nine billion possible DNA changes
friendlyTitle: DeepMind made a huge map of possible one-letter changes in human DNA
summary: Google DeepMind has released a free academic portal and API containing AlphaGenome predictions for every possible single-letter change in the human genome. The one-petabyte resource also introduces a combined variant-impact score, and collaborators report using it to prioritize variants later checked in rare-disease experiments.
friendlySummary: The free research tool predicts how nine billion small DNA changes may affect the body. Scientists can use a website or an API to search and rank possible effects.
whyItMatters: Precomputed predictions can let genetic researchers rank possible causes before committing scarce laboratory time. DeepMind explicitly says the atlas is not validated or approved for clinical use, so it should guide research questions rather than personal diagnosis or treatment.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This may help researchers decide what to test in the lab first. It is not a medical test and should not be used to diagnose or treat a person.
